findings.title: remove_member spec issues a PUT but the route only exists for DELETE
findings.body: The spec 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the new route in config/routes.rb only defines `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (PUT /admin/groups/members is mapped to add_members). There is no PUT route to Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, so this request raises an UrlGenerationError/routing error and the test will fail rather than asserting the intended 422. It must be `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` (as the other spec in the same context correctly uses).

findings.title: Pagination math is off by one, producing an empty phantom last page
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), totalPages becomes 3 even though there are only 2 pages, so `showingLast` never becomes true on the real last page. Combined with the `next` action clamping `offset` to `user_count` (line 33: `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), clicking next on the last real page sets offset to 100 and fetches an empty third page (currentPage 3/3 with no members). totalPages should use Math.ceil and offset should be clamped to the largest valid page start, not to user_count.

findings.title: PUT /admin/groups/:id silently drops membership updates from existing API consumers
findings.body: The old `update_put` action processed `params[:group][:usernames]` to replace group membership, and `update_patch` handled `params[:changes]` add/delete deltas (the PATCH route is also removed from config/routes.rb). The new `update` action only handles name/alias_level/visible, yet still returns success_json for a PUT containing a `group[usernames]` payload. Any existing API client, plugin, or script that manages memberships via PUT /admin/groups/:id will now get a 200 success while the membership change is silently ignored, with no error and no deprecation warning. Membership mutations should either still be accepted or rejected explicitly so consumers notice.

findings.title: create action ignores the alias_level parameter sent by the client
findings.body: The frontend Group#create (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) posts `asJSON()` which includes `alias_level`, but the server's create action only assigns `name` and `visible`. When an admin creates a new group with an alias level other than the default selected in the form, that setting is silently discarded and the group is created with alias_level 0; the admin only sees the correct value if they notice and save again. `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?` (as done in update) is missing from create.

findings.title: Public group members page now truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI
findings.body: Previously the public members endpoint returned all members for non-automatic groups (limit was only applied, with a default of 200, to automatic groups). Now `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` caps every group at 50 members, and the public group page (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) has no pagination controls, so the members list is silently cut off at 50 for larger groups. This is a user-visible regression: members 51+ are unreachable on the public group page. Either the template needs pagination like the admin page, or the default limit for the public route must not truncate.

findings.title: Unvalidated limit/offset parameters on the public members endpoint
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` are taken directly from params with no bounds validation. A client can request `/groups/<name>/members.json?limit=1000000` forcing serialization of the entire membership in one response (a cheap enumeration/DoS vector on large groups), and negative values (e.g. `limit=-1` or `offset=-5`) are passed straight into `.limit()/.offset()` which produces invalid SQL and a 500 error on PostgreSQL. The values should be clamped (e.g. limit between 1 and a max cap, offset >= 0).

findings.title: Save error handler crashes on non-JSON error responses
findings.body: In the `save` action's rejection handler, `$.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors` assumes the error body is always JSON containing an `errors` key. If the server returns a non-JSON body (e.g. a 500 HTML error page, a proxy timeout page, or an empty response), `$.parseJSON` throws and the user sees neither the real error message nor any feedback — the button just re-enables via .finally with no alert. The handler should fall back to a generic message when parsing fails or `errors` is absent.
